verdict_A.cancel: Source path holds the actual content-world cancel hook invoked by the sidepanel, releases the captured A target after B mounts, checks B overlay and distinct session, then detects, completes and extracts three rows. Native behavior has not run in this review.
verdict_A.install: Source path holds the actual sidepanel Chrome file-install promise, starts B while A is pending, releases A through the original Chrome call, checks same tab/document, exactly two installs and one start, then extracts B's three rows. Native behavior has not run in this review.
verdict_A.reinjection: Source path executes a second Chrome file installation and start for the current session, tracks capture-phase document listeners, checks one detection and three extracted rows. Fresh module-context identity is not established; native behavior has not run in this review.
verdict_A.stale_channels: Previously implemented EXIT, ITEM_DETECTED and RESULT cycles remain in the opt-in path ahead of the three new cases. They were not executed natively in this review.

findings.issue: Two recorded executeScript file calls and two start calls do not prove that the second installation created a distinct picker module context. A runtime that reuses the old module and calls mountListPicker again can satisfy overlay, listener, relay and extraction assertions, leaving the cross-context teardown regression untested.
findings.needed: At the content-world boundary, capture the installed start/teardown function identity before and after reinjection (or another direct module-context marker) and require the second identity to differ before crediting this case.

verdict_B.production_route: The new hooks wrap chrome.scripting.executeScript and the content-world __matrxListPickerCancel used by src/lib/data-pattern/list-picker-session.ts; they do not synthesize picker relays. The positive path checks stamped detection/result, one overlay, empty preselection root, field selection, and three extracted rows.
verdict_B.diagnostic: Lifecycle steps use fixed allowlisted targets and bounded count/boolean samples; the receipt preserves lifecycle_diagnostic.failed_target without raw exception, selector or page text. Probe tests exercise cancel, install and reinject serialization.

limits: No browser, native artifact, build, release or source edit was performed. The simulated boundary tests cannot establish a new Chrome module context or live behavior. Nonadmin role gating remains unverified.
recommended_next_action: Close the fresh-context proof gap in the runner, then run one resource-admitted hosted native acceptance against the exact installed artifact; keep D42 open pending nonadmin verification.
